quizPart1.question: Who wrote Never Let Me Go?
quizPart1.questionZh: 《Never Let Me Go》的作者是谁？
options: George Orwell
J. B. Priestley
Kazuo Ishiguro
William Golding
quizPart1.explanation: Kazuo Ishiguro is the author named in the supplied EPUB. The other writers are associated with different texts often studied at school.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 作者是石黑一雄（Kazuo Ishiguro）。注意不要与其他常见文学考试作家混淆；这是一道作品背景题，并不是叙述者身份题。
quizPart1.evidence: The supplied EPUB lists Kazuo Ishiguro as its creator.

quizPart1.question: In which year was the novel first published?
quizPart1.questionZh: 这部小说首次出版于哪一年？
quizPart1.explanation: The novel first appeared in 2005. The supplied Vintage EPUB records a 2006 edition date; an edition date is not necessarily the first-publication date.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 首次出版是2005年。你提供的Vintage电子书元数据标注2006年，这是该版本的日期，不能直接当成整部小说的首次出版年份。
quizPart1.evidence: The publisher and Morgan Library catalogue identify a 2005 original publication.

quizPart1.question: Which description best identifies the main childhood setting?
quizPart1.questionZh: 哪一项最准确地描述主人公的童年主要发生地？
options: Hailsham, a secluded school in the English countryside
A boarding school in central Tokyo
A hospital in New York
A university in London
optionsZh: Hailsham，英格兰乡间一所与外界隔离的学校
东京市中心的一所寄宿学校
quizPart1.explanation: The childhood memories centre on Hailsham and its English countryside surroundings. References to recovery centres belong to the adult narrative frame.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 童年回忆的核心地点是Hailsham，周围有田野和树林。开篇也提到成人时期的recovery centres，但它们不是童年学校的所在地。
quizPart1.evidence: The publisher describes the students in the English countryside; the chapters describe Hailsham’s fields and grounds.

quizPart1.question: Which term best describes Kathy’s way of telling the story?
quizPart1.questionZh: 哪个术语最准确地描述Kathy的叙述方式？
options: An omniscient third-person narrator
A diary written by Ruth at age eight
Retrospective first-person narration
A sequence of official school reports
quizPart1.explanation: An adult Kathy looks back on her own experiences. She can describe her observations and memories, but cannot directly access everyone else’s thoughts.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 成年Kathy回顾自己经历过的事，因此是retrospective first-person narration。她能观察、推测和回忆，却不能像全知叙述者那样直接知道所有人的内心。
quizPart1.evidence: The opening introduces Kathy in adulthood before she recalls her school years.

quizPart1.question: Why should we avoid treating the chapter order as a perfectly straight timeline?
quizPart1.questionZh: 为什么不能把章节顺序完全当成直线式时间顺序？
options: Every chapter is narrated by a different guardian
Kathy moves between memories and her adult present
The novel has no identifiable events
The chapters must be read in reverse order
optionsZh: Kathy会在不同回忆与成年现在之间转换
小说没有任何可辨认的事件
必须倒着阅读这些章节
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy follows associations, returns to earlier incidents, and comments from adulthood. Separate the time of an event from the time when she tells it.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Kathy常因某个物品、人物或话题联想到另一段记忆，然后再回来。复习时要区分“事情发生的时间”和“她讲述这件事的位置”，尤其注意Ch7的时间跳转。
quizPart1.evidence: The opening chapters repeatedly shift between adult caring work and different periods at Hailsham.

quizPart1.question: Which combination of literary forms best fits Chapters 1–9?
quizPart1.questionZh: 哪些文学形式的结合最适合描述第1—9章？
options: A coming-of-age story within a disturbing alternative society
A detective story that solves a murder in each chapter
A factual scientific manual about transplantation
A medieval historical epic narrated by a king
optionsZh: 成长故事与令人不安的架空社会相结合
每章侦破一起谋杀案的侦探故事
关于移植手术的科学说明书
由国王叙述的中世纪历史史诗
quizPart1.explanation: The chapters depict friendship, growing up and social pressure while gradually disclosing an invented donation system. The scientific premise serves a human story.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 可以用coming-of-age和dystopian/speculative fiction来理解：一方面是友谊、成长、从众；另一方面，普通学校生活逐渐显露出器官捐献制度的阴影。不要把它当成真实科学教材。
quizPart1.evidence: School memories and Miss Lucy’s explanation of the students’ predetermined futures combine familiar adolescence with an invented social system.

quizPart1.question: How old is Kathy when she introduces herself?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy在开篇自我介绍时几岁？
options: Thirteen
Thirty-one
Sixteen
Twenty-five
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy is thirty-one in the narrative present. Thirteen is associated with the school-age events recalled later in the opening chapters.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 开篇的Kathy是31岁，已经在做carer。13岁属于她随后回忆的Hailsham时期。题目问的是叙述当下，不是回忆中的年龄。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy states her age at the beginning of her account.

quizPart1.question: At the opening, approximately how long has Kathy already been a carer?
quizPart1.questionZh: 开篇时，Kathy已经做了多久的carer？
options: Exactly six months
Over eleven years
Only two years
Fourteen years
quizPart1.explanation: She has worked for over eleven years and expects to finish near twelve years. Fourteen years describes another carer; six years refers to her period of choosing donors.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 已经超过11年，预计年底结束时接近12年。14年说的是另一位carer；6年是她获准选择照顾对象的时间，并不是全部工作年限。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy distinguishes her total service from the last six years in which she has been allowed to choose donors.

quizPart1.question: What item particularly concerns Kathy during Tommy’s tantrum?
quizPart1.questionZh: Tommy发脾气时，Kathy特别担心他的哪件东西？
options: His favourite light blue polo shirt
His new red school tie
His leather pencil case
His football boots signed by a player
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy notices that mud could spoil his prized polo shirt, bought at a Sale. Her attention to its personal value helps distinguish her response from the spectators’ mockery.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是Tommy珍爱的浅蓝色polo衫，来自Sale。Kathy关注的不是“衣服贵不贵”，而是它对Tommy的重要性；这让她的反应与其他人的旁观嘲笑有所区别。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy warns Tommy that his favourite light blue polo shirt will get muddy.

quizPart1.question: Why is Tommy left out during the football team selection?
quizPart1.questionZh: 足球分队时，Tommy为什么被留到最后，最终遭到排斥？
options: He is clearly the worst footballer
A guardian forbids him to play
The boys deliberately organise his humiliation
He refuses to join either team
optionsZh: 男孩们故意安排这一幕来羞辱他
quizPart1.explanation: The exclusion is a planned provocation, despite Tommy’s ability at football. His anger follows humiliation; it is not evidence that he cannot play.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 这是其他男孩蓄意的羞辱，并非正常的按水平选人。文本还强调Tommy球技很好。分析时应看到“先被排斥—再爆发”的因果，不能只把他写成无缘无故发怒。
quizPart1.evidence: The watchers know about the plot, while Kathy recalls that Tommy is an excellent football player.

quizPart1.question: How does Kathy understand Tommy’s blow to her face?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy如何理解Tommy打到她脸的那一下？
options: As an accidental result of his flailing arm
As a carefully planned attack on her
As punishment ordered by Ruth
As part of an organised boxing lesson
optionsZh: 他挥动手臂时造成的意外
他精心计划对她的袭击
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy believes it was unintentional: she touches his arm while he is still thrashing about. Tommy’s later apology supports this account without excusing his whole outburst.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Kathy认为那是意外：她伸手碰他时，他还在乱挥手臂。要区分“碰伤Kathy是否故意”与“他的情绪失控是否造成影响”，不能把两者混为一谈。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy says she was fairly sure Tommy did not intend to hit her.

quizPart1.question: What does Laura’s imitation of Tommy’s changing expressions reveal most clearly?
quizPart1.questionZh: Laura模仿Tommy不断变化的表情，最清楚地揭示了什么？
options: Laura secretly controls the football rules
His distress becomes entertainment for the watching group
The girls fully understand Tommy’s private thoughts
Every observer has identical feelings throughout
optionsZh: 他的痛苦变成旁观群体的娱乐
女孩们完全知道Tommy内心在想什么
所有旁观者从头到尾都抱有完全一样的感受
quizPart1.explanation: Laura’s performance prompts laughter while Tommy moves from hope to humiliation. Kathy’s discomfort complicates the group response, so the scene does not prove that all witnesses feel exactly alike.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Laura的模仿让Tommy从期待到受辱的过程成为笑料。这体现群体旁观的残酷；但Kathy又有犹豫与关心，因此不能把所有旁观者简单写成完全一样。
quizPart1.evidence: Laura imitates Tommy as the girls watch the team selection and laugh.

quizPart1.question: Which nurse do the students nickname Crow Face?
quizPart1.questionZh: 学生把哪位护士称为Crow Face？
options: Miss Jody
Miss Lucy
Miss Geraldine
Nurse Trisha
quizPart1.explanation: Nurse Trisha conducts the frequent medical examinations and is nicknamed Crow Face. Miss Jody is mentioned in connection with cleaning Tommy’s shirt.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Crow Face指Nurse Trisha。她负责频繁的身体检查。Miss Jody则出现在Kathy建议处理Tommy脏衣服的情节中，不要只凭相似的称呼混淆人物。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy describes weekly medical examinations with Nurse Trisha, known among students as Crow Face.

quizPart1.question: What did Tommy paint in the art-class incident linked to the start of his difficulties?
quizPart1.questionZh: 与Tommy遭受嘲弄的开端有关的那幅画，画的是什么？
options: A horse beside a stable
A portrait of Madame
An elephant in tall grass
A boat on a river
quizPart1.explanation: Tommy produces a deliberately childish-looking watercolour of an elephant. Do not confuse this early painting with Ruth’s imaginary horses or later artistic developments.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是高草中的大象水彩画。画得显得比他的年龄幼稚；Ruth的马是另一个情节中的想象游戏，不是这幅画的内容。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 2 · Tommy recalls an art lesson
quizPart1.evidence: Tommy identifies an elephant watercolour in Miss Geraldine’s class as a turning point.

quizPart1.question: Why does Miss Geraldine’s response to the elephant painting have an ironic result?
quizPart1.questionZh: Miss Geraldine对大象画的反应为什么具有反讽意味？
options: Her harsh punishment immediately makes Tommy popular
She ignores the painting and it wins a prize outside school
She asks every student to paint the same elephant
Her protective praise helps provoke resentment against Tommy
optionsZh: 她的严厉惩罚立刻使Tommy受欢迎
她无视画作，作品却在校外获奖
她让全体学生画同一头大象
她想保护他的表扬反而激起其他人对他的不满
quizPart1.explanation: Miss Geraldine tries to be kind by finding qualities to praise. Kathy suggests that this draws attention to the poor painting and fuels resentment: intention and effect diverge.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 她本意是温柔地保护Tommy，因此努力找优点表扬；效果却是让别人更注意到画作的问题并产生不满。反讽在于善意的intention与实际effect并不一致。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy links the guardian’s unusually generous praise to the resentment that followed.

quizPart1.question: How often are the Hailsham Exchanges held?
quizPart1.questionZh: Hailsham的Exchanges多久举行一次？
options: Once a month
Every week
Only once when students leave
Four times a year, one per season
quizPart1.explanation: The Exchanges happen in spring, summer, autumn and winter. The monthly arrival of outside goods belongs to the Sales system described in Chapter 4.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Exchanges每年春、夏、秋、冬各一次，交换的是学生作品。每月运来外界物品的是Sales相关安排，考试很容易把这两种活动的频率混在一起。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy lists four seasonal Exchanges each year.

quizPart1.question: What does Christy’s reputation for poetry illustrate?
quizPart1.questionZh: Christy因诗歌获得的声望说明了什么？
options: Every student is an expert literary critic
Ruth has no influence over any student
Creative reputation can shape social authority even without real understanding
Poetry is excluded from Exchanges
optionsZh: 所有学生都是专业文学评论家
Ruth对任何学生都没有影响力
即使同学并不真正懂诗，创作声誉也能带来社会地位
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy remembers that even Ruth would not readily boss Christy about. The students respected her poetry although Kathy questions how much they actually understood or cared about poetry.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Kathy指出，连Ruth也不太敢指使Christy；但他们当时未必真正懂诗、爱诗。这揭示“被认可的creativity”如何转化成群体中的地位，而不只是审美欣赏。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy contrasts Christy’s high status with the students’ limited understanding of poetry.

quizPart1.question: What change in Tommy begins before the bullying fades?
quizPart1.questionZh: 在欺凌逐渐减少之前，Tommy先发生了什么变化？
options: He suddenly becomes the school’s best artist
He leaves Hailsham permanently
He becomes the head guardian’s assistant
He begins controlling his temper and responding more calmly
optionsZh: 他突然成为全校最好的艺术家
他开始控制脾气，更平静地回应挑衅
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy notices that the pranks initially continue but no longer reliably produce tantrums. His art reputation has not suddenly improved, so artistic success is not the explanation.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 恶作剧最初仍在继续，但Tommy不再总是爆发，其他人渐渐失去兴趣。他的艺术名声并没有突然改善；真正要追问的是他为何获得了不同的自我感受。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy observes a calmer response before the teasing becomes less frequent.

quizPart1.question: Where do Kathy and Tommy discuss Miss Lucy’s unusual advice in detail?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy和Tommy在哪里详细谈论Miss Lucy的反常建议？
options: Beside the pond
Inside Miss Emily’s office
At the centre of the Dining Hall during a Sale
In the woods beyond Hailsham
quizPart1.explanation: They speak beside the pond, away from the busiest areas. The earlier lunch queue helps them arrange the conversation; it is not the main setting of this extended discussion.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 这段深入谈话发生在池塘旁。午餐排队与他们安排交谈有关，但不要把“安排谈话的地点”和“长谈本身的地点”混淆。
quizPart1.evidence: Tommy sits on a rock near the pond while Kathy questions him about Miss Lucy.

quizPart1.question: What had Miss Lucy told Tommy about his lack of creativity?
quizPart1.questionZh: Miss Lucy最初对Tommy缺乏创造力的问题说了什么？
options: He must win every Exchange to stay at Hailsham
He should abandon all school subjects immediately
If he has genuinely tried, he should not be blamed for finding creativity difficult
The other students are correct to punish him
optionsZh: 他必须在每次Exchange获胜才能留校
他应立刻放弃所有学科
只要他确实努力过，就不该因创作困难而受责备
其他学生惩罚他是正确的
quizPart1.explanation: Her reassurance challenges the assumption that poor creative performance makes him a bad student. It helps him stop treating the bullying as proof of his own worthlessness.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 她说，真正努力过却难以创作，并不是他的过错，也不应成为被惩罚的理由。这挑战了“艺术不好＝学生不好”的评价方式，让Tommy不再把欺凌完全归咎于自己。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 3 · Tommy reports Miss Lucy’s reassurance
quizPart1.evidence: Miss Lucy separates Tommy’s value as a student from his artistic achievement.

quizPart1.question: Which child once praises young Kathy’s modelling work as good enough for the Gallery?
quizPart1.questionZh: 哪个孩子曾说年幼Kathy的泥塑好到可以进Gallery？
options: Amanda C.
Midge A.
Charlotte F.
Moira B.
quizPart1.explanation: Amanda C., a year older, makes the comment while they work with modelling clay. The memory shows how early the Gallery already structures the children’s ambitions.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是大一岁的Amanda C.。这段小回忆说明，Gallery作为一种认可标准，早早就进入了孩子们的想象；他们未必知道其真实用途，却已渴望获得肯定。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 3 · Early memory of modelling clay
quizPart1.evidence: Amanda C. praises Kathy’s clay work and mentions the Gallery.

quizPart1.question: Which appearance is associated with Madame’s visits?
quizPart1.questionZh: Madame来访时，哪项外貌描述与原文相符？
options: A nurse’s uniform and long red hair
A purple satin dress identical to Judy’s
A football shirt covered in mud
A sharp grey suit and short hair
optionsZh: 利落的灰色套装和短发
quizPart1.explanation: Madame is described in a grey suit, with short hair and a distant manner. The purple satin dress belongs to the image on Kathy’s Judy Bridgewater cassette cover.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Madame穿灰色套装、留短发，态度疏离。紫色缎面裙属于Judy Bridgewater磁带封面的形象，不是Madame来学校时的穿着。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy describes Madame as a narrow, short-haired woman in a sharp grey suit.

quizPart1.question: What makes the children’s test of Madame especially disturbing?
quizPart1.questionZh: 孩子们试探Madame之后，为什么深受震动？
options: She loudly announces that she will expel them
They experience her fear of them as if they were repellent creatures
She takes away all their tokens as a punishment
They learn that she cannot recognise any artwork
optionsZh: 她大声宣布要开除他们
他们感到她像害怕令人厌恶的生物那样害怕他们
他们得知她认不出任何艺术品
quizPart1.explanation: Madame freezes and seems afraid of physical contact. Kathy compares the feeling to being seen as spiders; the shock concerns how an outsider perceives their very existence.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Madame没有大喊大叫，却僵住、害怕被碰到。Kathy把这种目光比作人看蜘蛛的恐惧；刺痛他们的不是一条惩罚规定，而是第一次感到“别人眼中的我们”竟如此陌生。
quizPart1.evidence: The children move around Madame and notice her suppressed shudder and dread of being touched.

quizPart1.question: What do the students actually know about the Gallery at this stage?
quizPart1.questionZh: 到第3章为止，学生真正知道Gallery的哪些情况？
options: Madame takes selected work, but its destination and purpose remain uncertain
They have all visited it and know its full purpose
They know that every object is sold back to their parents
A guardian has publicly explained every rule governing it
optionsZh: Madame拿走精选作品，但去向和用途仍不清楚
他们都参观过，完全了解用途
他们知道所有物品都会卖回父母手中
guardian已公开解释其所有规则
quizPart1.explanation: They treat the Gallery as familiar but cannot explain it securely. Distinguish observed fact—Madame selects work—from inherited assumptions about what happens afterwards.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 可以确定的是Madame确实挑选并带走作品；Gallery是什么、为什么存在，他们并没有可靠答案。要把observed fact与学生群体传下来的assumption分开。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy says everyone spoke of the Gallery although nobody knew for sure what it was.

quizPart1.question: Which student approaches Miss Emily about compensation for work taken by Madame?
quizPart1.questionZh: 哪位学生去找Miss Emily，提出作品被Madame拿走后应获得补偿？
options: Christopher H.
Harry C.
Roy J.
Peter J.
quizPart1.explanation: Roy J. has already had several items selected and takes the concern to the head guardian. The outcome is a small number of tokens, not unrestricted payment.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是Roy J.，他已有多件作品被选走。最后学校同意给少量tokens，同时仍强调被选中是一种荣誉；不是完全按学生要求补偿。
quizPart1.evidence: Roy J. goes to Miss Emily after students argue about receiving tokens for Madame’s selections.

quizPart1.question: Which imaginary horse does Ruth first assign to Kathy, with a warning not to use a crop?
quizPart1.questionZh: Ruth最初让Kathy骑哪匹想象中的马，并叮嘱不能用马鞭？
options: Thunder
Bramble
Daffodil
Pegasus
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy first takes Bramble. Ruth initially says Thunder is too dangerous; Kathy is allowed to try him only later in the game.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 先骑的是Bramble，而且不能对它使用crop（马鞭）。Thunder最初被说成太危险，后来Kathy才获准尝试。先后顺序是这道题的关键。
quizPart1.evidence: Ruth offers Bramble and repeats the instruction not to use a crop.

quizPart1.question: Which statement about Thunder is accurate?
quizPart1.questionZh: 关于Thunder，哪项说法准确？
options: He is Ruth’s favourite, initially withheld but eventually ridden by Kathy
He is a real school horse that Kathy never sees
He belongs to Miss Geraldine and is sold at a Sale
He is the first horse Ruth assigns before mentioning Bramble
optionsZh: 它是Ruth最喜欢的马，起初不让Kathy骑，后来让她骑了
它是学校的一匹真马，Kathy从未见过
它属于Miss Geraldine，后来在Sale被卖掉
Ruth在提到Bramble之前就先让Kathy骑它
quizPart1.explanation: Thunder is Ruth’s best/favourite imaginary horse. The important correction is that her initial refusal is not permanent: Kathy eventually gets a turn.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Thunder是Ruth最好的、最喜欢的想象中的马。容易错在把“起初拒绝”记成“始终不让骑”；原文明确说Kathy后来也骑了Thunder。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 4 · Changing permission within the horse game
quizPart1.evidence: Ruth first withholds Thunder as dangerous, then eventually lets Kathy try him.

quizPart1.question: What instruction does Ruth give Kathy about Daffodil?
quizPart1.questionZh: Ruth要求Kathy骑Daffodil时怎样做？
options: Use the crop constantly
Stand in the saddle with eyes closed
Walk away and never ride her
Lean far back
quizPart1.explanation: Ruth insists that Kathy lean well back because Daffodil dislikes anything else. The changing instructions make Ruth the authority inside their shared imaginary world.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Ruth要求Kathy向后仰得更多，说Daffodil不喜欢别的姿势。除了记名字，也可看出Ruth通过规定每匹马的“脾气”掌握游戏规则。
quizPart1.evidence: Ruth calls out a specific instruction to lean back while Kathy rides Daffodil.

quizPart1.question: What chiefly distinguishes the Sales from the Exchanges?
quizPart1.questionZh: Sales与Exchanges最主要的区别是什么？
options: Sales are secret meetings; Exchanges are medical examinations
Sales offer goods brought from outside; Exchanges centre on students’ creations
Sales happen only after leaving; Exchanges happen only in infancy
Sales use pounds; Exchanges use no currency at all
optionsZh: Sales出售外界带来的物品；Exchanges以学生作品为主
Sales离校后才有；Exchanges只在幼儿时期举行
quizPart1.explanation: Both help students build collections, but the source of the objects differs. Outside clothes, toys and tapes arrive for Sales; creative work circulates through Exchanges.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 两者都帮助学生建立个人collection，但物品来源不同。Sales是外界运来的衣服、玩具、磁带等；Exchanges是学生创作的画、诗、手工等，不要混成同一种活动。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 4 · Outside goods and monthly deliveries
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy contrasts outside goods at Sales with the students’ work at Exchanges.

quizPart1.question: What does the imaginary-horse episode reveal about Ruth and Kathy’s friendship?
quizPart1.questionZh: 想象中的马这一情节，如何展示Ruth与Kathy的友谊？
options: Kathy rejects imaginative play from the beginning
Ruth has no interest in being accepted by anyone
The friendship is based only on buying real animals
Shared pleasure develops alongside Ruth’s control over rules and access
optionsZh: Kathy从一开始就拒绝想象游戏
Ruth完全不在乎他人的接受
友谊完全建立在购买真实动物上
共同的快乐与Ruth对规则、资格的控制同时出现
quizPart1.explanation: They genuinely lose themselves in play, but Ruth determines which horses Kathy may ride and abruptly ends the game. Affection and unequal power coexist.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 她们确实沉浸在游戏里、获得快乐；与此同时，Ruth决定能骑哪匹马、怎样骑、何时结束。分析不要只写“友谊虚假”或“Ruth坏”，而要看亲密与权力如何并存。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy enjoys Ruth’s invitation, while Ruth controls permissions and ends the game by accusing Kathy of tiring the horses.

quizPart1.question: Whom does the secret guard claim to protect?
quizPart1.questionZh: secret guard声称要保护谁？
options: Miss Geraldine
Madame
Nurse Trisha
Miss Emily
quizPart1.explanation: The imaginary plot centres on Miss Geraldine being abducted. The guard gathers supposed evidence but avoids telling her or directly confronting the alleged conspirators.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 他们声称要保护Miss Geraldine，防止她被绑架。这个组织主要不断收集所谓证据，却避免真正对质或告诉她，说明游戏的维持比实际行动更重要。
quizPart1.evidence: Ruth’s group imagines a plot to abduct Miss Geraldine and treats several people as conspirators.

quizPart1.question: What false rule does Ruth give when pretending to teach chess?
quizPart1.questionZh: Ruth装作会下棋时，教了哪条错误规则？
options: Every piece moves in an L-shape
Every piece can move only one square forward
The king must remain outside the board
Players must swap colours after every move
optionsZh: 每种棋子只能向前一格
国王必须一直放在棋盘外
每下一步双方必须交换颜色
quizPart1.explanation: Ruth seems to have generalised the knight’s move to all pieces. Kathy’s disappointment exposes the gap between Ruth’s confident performance and her actual knowledge.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Ruth似乎把knight（马）的走法推广给全部棋子。Kathy意识到她并不真正懂棋；重点是Ruth表现出的expertise与实际知识之间存在落差。
quizPart1.evidence: Ruth describes an L-shaped movement for every piece and disputes Kathy’s supposedly too-straight move.

quizPart1.question: Which expelled guard member calls the secret guard childish, provoking Kathy’s defence?
quizPart1.questionZh: 哪位被逐出secret guard的成员批评游戏幼稚，却引来Kathy强烈维护？
options: Midge A.
Amanda C.
Charlotte F.
Moira B.
quizPart1.explanation: Moira B. could have been Kathy’s ally after both were excluded. Instead, Kathy angrily defends the shared fantasy and invents personal evidence for it.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是Moira B.。两人都曾受排斥，本可同病相怜，但Kathy反而愤怒维护游戏，甚至编造自己亲耳听见阴谋。这说明依恋群体未必符合表面的利益逻辑。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 5 · Kathy and Moira in the courtyard
quizPart1.evidence: Moira criticises the secret guard, and Kathy claims to have overheard the kidnapping plan herself.

quizPart1.question: Which monitor does Kathy name in her story about looking at the Sales Register?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy声称查看Sales Register时，提到了哪位monitor？
options: Christopher H.
Mr. Christopher
Roy J.
Christopher C.
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy names Christopher C. in her bluff. Christopher H. is the student associated with the elbow story in Chapter 7; the initials matter.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是Christopher C.。Christopher H.在第7章编造“肘部会拉开”的故事，Mr. Christopher则是成人guardian。遇到同名人物，要连首字母和身份一起记。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy says Christopher C. was a monitor while she pretended to browse the Sales Register.

quizPart1.question: How does Kathy actually challenge Ruth’s implied story about the pencil case?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy实际上怎样挑战Ruth关于笔袋来源的暗示？
options: She produces a signed confession from Miss Geraldine
She bluffs that she has looked through the Sales Register
She buys the same pencil case from Madame
She steals Ruth’s collection chest and opens it
optionsZh: 她拿出Miss Geraldine签名的承认书
她虚张声势，声称自己看过Sales Register
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy realises she need not complete the investigation if Ruth believes she has checked the record. The narrative presents a bluff, not documentary proof shown to the group.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Kathy只是bluff：让Ruth以为自己查过记录。她没有拿出实际登记证据。复习要分清“她考虑过的计划”与“最后真正做出的行动”。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy decides that bluffing about the register is enough and tells Ruth she has browsed it.

quizPart1.question: Why does Kathy feel regret when Ruth nearly cries over the pencil case?
quizPart1.questionZh: Ruth因笔袋事件几乎落泪时，Kathy为什么后悔？
options: She suddenly discovers the pencil case is dangerous
She recognises a friend’s vulnerable wish to feel specially loved
She learns Ruth has been ordered to leave Hailsham
She remembers she has never met Miss Geraldine
optionsZh: 她突然发现笔袋有危险
她意识到朋友脆弱地渴望被特别关爱
她想起自己从未见过Miss Geraldine
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy’s imagined triumph becomes the reality of hurting her friend. She understands Ruth’s claim as an intensified version of a shared longing for special affection.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 原本想象中的“揭穿胜利”，变成眼前朋友真实的受伤。Kathy想到她们都希望guardian特别喜欢自己；这让Ruth的炫耀显出脆弱，也使Kathy反思自己的残忍。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 5 · The emotional aftermath of the bluff
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy is shocked by Ruth’s distress and recognises the common wish for a guardian’s special affection.

quizPart1.question: Which pairing correctly identifies Kathy’s treasured cassette?
quizPart1.questionZh: 哪组“专辑名—歌手”正确对应Kathy珍爱的磁带？
options: Songs After Dark — Judy Bridgewater
Twenty Classic Dance Tunes — Judy Bridgewater
Never Let Me Go — Miss Geraldine
Songs After Dark — Miss Lucy
quizPart1.explanation: Songs After Dark is the cassette/album title and Judy Bridgewater is the singer. Never Let Me Go is the particular song; the dance-tunes tape is Ruth’s later gift.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Songs After Dark是专辑名，Judy Bridgewater是歌手，Never Let Me Go是其中的歌曲。Twenty Classic Dance Tunes则是Ruth后来送的另一盘磁带。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy names her cassette Songs After Dark by Judy Bridgewater.

quizPart1.question: Which track on Kathy’s cassette is Never Let Me Go?
quizPart1.questionZh: Never Let Me Go是Kathy那盘磁带的第几首？
options: Track three
Track one
Track six
Track twelve
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy singles out track three and tries to keep the tape ready at that point. The precise detail shows repeated, private listening rather than general enthusiasm for the whole album.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是track number three。她常把磁带停在这一位置，好随时播放。这个细节强调她与一首特定歌曲的私人情感，而不是对整盘音乐都同样喜爱。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy identifies the song as track three and describes keeping the tape wound to it.

quizPart1.question: Why does Kathy turn the cassette cover inside out?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy为什么把磁带封面翻到里面？
options: The cover shows a map of the forbidden woods
Ruth has written her own name across it
Madame has forbidden every picture of a singer
The cover shows Judy holding a cigarette
optionsZh: 封面画了禁入树林的地图
Ruth在上面写满了自己的名字
封面上的Judy手里拿着香烟
quizPart1.explanation: The cigarette makes Kathy secretive because smoking is heavily condemned at Hailsham. The cover is not evidence that Kathy herself smokes.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 原因是封面有香烟，而Hailsham极严厉地反对吸烟。注意：Kathy隐藏的是图片，不代表她自己吸烟。学校对身体健康的强调使这个小图像都显得敏感。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy hides the cover because Judy is pictured with a burning cigarette.

quizPart1.question: What is Kathy doing when Madame sees her and cries?
quizPart1.questionZh: Madame看见Kathy并哭泣时，Kathy正在做什么？
options: Presenting a painting at an Exchange
Arguing with Ruth about a chessboard
Swaying to the song while holding a pillow as an imagined baby
Trying to climb the school fence
optionsZh: 随歌曲摇摆，抱着枕头想象那是婴儿
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy uses the pillow in her private interpretation of the song. Madame’s tears are observed, but their full meaning is not established for the children at this stage.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Kathy把枕头想象成婴儿，跟着歌慢慢摇摆。到这里能够确定的是Madame看见并哭了；她为什么哭，孩子们并没有得到完整、可靠的解释，不应把猜测当事实。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy discovers Madame at the doorway while dancing with a pillow held to her breast.

quizPart1.question: Why does Norfolk become emotionally important to the children?
quizPart1.questionZh: 为什么Norfolk对孩子们有特殊的情感意义？
options: They imagine lost possessions may be recoverable there
They have documentary proof that all stolen goods go there
It is the only place where guardians may live
It is the official name of their medical programme
optionsZh: 他们想象丢失的珍贵物品也许可以在那里找回
他们有证据证明所有失窃物品都会运往那里
那是唯一允许guardians居住的地方
那是他们医疗计划的官方名称
quizPart1.explanation: A geographical description develops into a comforting fantasy about a national lost-property corner. Its emotional usefulness matters more to them than checking whether it is logical.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 他们把地理课上的“失落角落”发展成一种幻想：珍贵之物不是彻底消失，而是去了Norfolk。它提供的是loss中的comfort，并不是经核实的现实规律。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 6 · Norfolk as a place for lost things
quizPart1.evidence: The children connect Norfolk with the lost-property idea and take comfort in imagining future recovery.

quizPart1.question: What replacement gift does Ruth give Kathy after the cassette disappears?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy的磁带丢失后，Ruth送她什么作为替代礼物？
options: Another copy of Songs After Dark
A new Walkman with no tape
Twenty Classic Dance Tunes
A recording of Miss Emily’s speeches
quizPart1.explanation: Ruth gives a different recording containing ballroom-dance music. Kathy values the gesture of care, even though it is not the music she lost.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Ruth送的是另一盘磁带Twenty Classic Dance Tunes，内容是舞厅舞曲。它没有真正替回原来的音乐，但Kathy珍视朋友用心补偿的举动；物品的意义来自关系。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 6 · Ruth’s gift on the hill
quizPart1.evidence: Ruth explains that she could not find the lost tape and offers a different recording bought at a Sale.

quizPart1.question: Which two boys’ conversation prompts Miss Lucy to interrupt on the pavilion veranda?
quizPart1.questionZh: 哪两个男孩在亭子走廊上的谈话，引发了Miss Lucy的打断？
options: Christopher C. and Roy J.
Tommy and Harry C.
Peter J. and Gordon
Gary B. and Arthur H.
quizPart1.explanation: Peter J. is talking to Gordon about becoming actors, with America offering the best chance. Miss Lucy responds to this imagined future rather than merely to noisy behaviour.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是Peter J.与Gordon，话题是当演员以及去美国的机会。Miss Lucy的反应针对他们想象中的未来，不只是因为他们吵闹或不守纪律。
quizPart1.evidence: Miss Lucy asks Peter to repeat what he was saying to Gordon about an acting career.

quizPart1.question: How old are the students during Miss Lucy’s direct speech about their futures?
quizPart1.questionZh: Miss Lucy在亭子走廊直接说明未来时，学生们大约几岁？
options: Eight
Ten
Fifteen
Thirty-one
quizPart1.explanation: They are fifteen and in their final Hailsham year. The chapter also recalls events at thirteen, so not every scene in Chapter 7 happens at the same age.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 这次讲话发生在15岁、Hailsham最后一年。第7章也回顾了13岁时的事情，所以不能因为同在一章，就把所有事件都放在同一年龄。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy locates the veranda speech when the students are fifteen.

quizPart1.question: What central fact does Miss Lucy insist they face?
quizPart1.questionZh: Miss Lucy坚持让他们直面的核心事实是什么？
options: They may choose any profession after a final examination
Every student will become a guardian at Hailsham
Their assigned futures involve donating vital organs before middle age
Their future depends only on who wins at rounders
optionsZh: 通过期末考试后他们可以自由选择任何职业
他们被安排在未到中年时开始捐献重要器官
他们的未来只取决于谁赢得rounders比赛
quizPart1.explanation: She directly rejects ordinary career expectations and describes a predetermined purpose. She is making the implications explicit, not offering a new career option.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 她否定演员、超市工作等普通职业想象，说明他们的未来早已被安排。重点是让学生真正面对已有信息的后果，而不是介绍一种可自由选择的职业。
quizPart1.evidence: Miss Lucy states that the students were created for donations and that their futures have already been decided.

quizPart1.question: Who starts the claim that Tommy’s injured elbow might unzip?
quizPart1.questionZh: 谁最先声称Tommy受伤的肘部可能像拉链一样打开？
options: Christopher C.
Nurse Trisha
Miss Emily
Christopher H.
quizPart1.explanation: Christopher H., a student from the year above, presents the invented danger seriously. It is a prank, not a medical warning from Crow Face.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是高一届的Christopher H.，他说得一本正经，其他人又跟着附和。它是恶作剧，不是Nurse Trisha的医学警告；Christopher C.则是笔袋事件里的monitor。
quizPart1.evidence: Christopher H. warns Tommy at lunch that bending the injured elbow could make it open up.

quizPart1.question: What does being told and not told mean most precisely?
quizPart1.questionZh: “told and not told”最准确的含义是什么？
options: The students have literally never heard the word donation
Miss Lucy gives them contradictory dates for an examination
Every student understands the whole system but refuses all care
The students possess information without fully grasping its implications
optionsZh: Miss Lucy告诉他们互相矛盾的考试日期
每人都完全理解制度并拒绝一切照顾
学生听过事实，却未充分理解其后果
quizPart1.explanation: Awareness is not the same as understanding. Timing, embarrassment, distraction and habits of avoidance can keep known facts emotionally distant.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 核心区别是knowing the facts与understanding the implications。信息可能早已进入脑中，却因年幼、羞耻、分心和回避而没有被认真消化；不是简单的“从未被告知”。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 7 · Reflecting on Miss Lucy’s phrase
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy and Tommy consider how familiar information could remain insufficiently understood.

quizPart1.question: How does Kathy describe the change after Miss Lucy’s speech?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy怎样描述Miss Lucy讲话之后的变化？
options: Everyone immediately organises an escape
Donation jokes fade and the subject becomes serious and sombre
The students forget every earlier warning
Donations become an ordinary topic discussed freely all day
optionsZh: 捐献玩笑减少，这个话题变得严肃沉重
学生忘记所有以前的警告
捐献成为大家整天自由讨论的普通话题
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy says the joking diminishes and avoidance returns in a more serious form. The shift suggests greater recognition, but not unrestricted discussion or collective action.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 玩笑逐渐消失，但并不等于大家开始充分讨论。回避仍在，只是从原来的尴尬变成更沉重的沉默：有所认识，不等于已经能直接面对或采取行动。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 7 · The aftermath of the speech
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy describes the donation subject becoming sombre rather than the focus of jokes.

quizPart1.question: In which room does Kathy find Miss Lucy angrily covering pages?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy在哪间教室发现Miss Lucy愤怒地涂划纸张？
options: Room 18
Room 22
Room 5
The Dining Hall
quizPart1.explanation: The incident occurs in small, dim Room 22. Room 18 is associated with medical checks, and Room 5 with the earlier pencil-case display.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是狭小、昏暗的Room 22。Room 18与体检有关，Room 5则是早先展示笔袋的教室。地点细节最好与事件成对记忆。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy follows a repeated hissing noise to Room 22 and discovers Miss Lucy.

quizPart1.question: What is Miss Lucy actually doing when Kathy hears the hissing sound?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy听到嘶嘶声时，Miss Lucy实际上在做什么？
options: Repairing a leaking gas pipe
Playing a damaged cassette
Scrubbing pencil lines over neat blue handwriting
Burning the students’ paintings
optionsZh: 用铅笔猛烈涂黑原本整齐的蓝色字迹
quizPart1.explanation: The noise comes from her pencil moving furiously across paper. Kathy observes the action and her flushed face, but does not learn exactly what the writing contained.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 声音来自铅笔猛烈摩擦纸面。Kathy看见原本整齐的蓝字被覆盖，却不知道具体内容。分析可以讨论压抑或冲突，但不能声称自己知道她正在销毁哪份文件。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy sees heavy black lines being drawn over blue handwriting.

quizPart1.question: Who makes the small calendar that Kathy proudly shows Tommy?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy骄傲地拿给Tommy看的小日历是谁制作的？
options: Patricia C.
Christy
Amanda C.
Miss Emily
quizPart1.explanation: Patricia C.’s calendar contains pencil sketches of Hailsham life. It is different from Miss Emily’s county calendars and from Christy’s celebrated poetry.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是Patricia C.制作的，里面画着Hailsham生活的铅笔小画。它不同于Miss Emily展示各郡的彩色日历，也不是Christy的诗集。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 8 · The calendar beside the sycamore
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy shows Tommy a calendar of Hailsham scenes made by Patricia C.

quizPart1.question: Which boy does Kathy consider approaching because she sees him as experienced, quiet and discreet?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy认为哪个男孩有经验、安静而不会到处议论，因此考虑与他接近？
options: Harry C.
Roy J.
Christopher H.
Arthur H.
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy selects Harry C. partly because she expects him to be considerate and unlikely to gossip. Her choice also reflects anxiety about experience and social expectations.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是Harry C.。Kathy觉得他较体贴、不会散播私事。这段情节既显示她试图谨慎掌控自己的选择，也暴露她对同伴经验和群体期待的焦虑。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 8 · Kathy’s plans and social pressure
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy explains that Harry seems decent, quiet and unlikely to gossip.

quizPart1.question: Why is Tommy’s angry response to Laura’s comment about mud significant?
quizPart1.questionZh: Tommy对Laura指出他衣服上有泥的玩笑反应强烈，为什么值得注意？
options: It proves Laura has deliberately resumed a long bullying campaign
It suggests renewed inner distress that Kathy initially misreads
It proves Tommy has become a guardian
It proves the mud contains dangerous chemicals
optionsZh: 它证明Laura故意重启长期欺凌计划
它提示Tommy内心又出现困扰，但Kathy起初理解错了
它证明泥里含危险化学物质
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy presents the comment as friendly teasing but is surprised by Tommy’s intensity. She initially associates his difficulties with relationship trouble, overlooking other possible causes.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Kathy把这次玩笑描述为友好的打趣，因此Tommy强烈的反应显得异常。她最初只从恋爱冲突理解他的情绪，忽视了另有原因的可能，体现叙述者认识的局限。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 8 · Laura notices mud on Tommy’s shirt
quizPart1.evidence: Tommy abruptly turns on Laura’s friendly remark and then stalks away.

quizPart1.question: How does Kathy connect adolescent pressure about experience with earlier pressure about creativity?
quizPart1.questionZh: Kathy怎样把青春期的“经验压力”与早年的creativity压力联系起来？
options: Both are official competitive school examinations
Both guarantee that rumours are always true
Both make the students completely independent of others
Both can become tests of belonging and social worth
optionsZh: 两者都是正式的竞争性学校考试
两者都证明传言一定真实
两者都使学生彻底不受他人影响
两者都可能成为衡量归属感与个人价值的群体标准
quizPart1.explanation: Kathy feels that being inexperienced marks her out, much as poor creativity previously affected status. She also questions whether classmates’ confident claims are reliable.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 她觉得没有经验会显得落后，正如以前“不够有创造力”会损害地位。这种比较揭示peer pressure；同时她也怀疑同学的自信宣称，不应把所有吹嘘当作事实。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 8 · Growing up and fitting in
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy explicitly compares the new pressure to earlier expectations about being creative.

quizPart1.question: Who first calls Kathy Tommy’s natural successor after his break-up with Ruth?
quizPart1.questionZh: Tommy与Ruth分手后，谁先说Kathy会自然接替Ruth的位置？
options: Charlotte F.
Cynthia E.
Midge A.
Miss Lucy
quizPart1.explanation: Cynthia E. makes the remark in the Art Room. Hannah later hints at a similar assumption; the initial explicit comment comes from Cynthia.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 是Cynthia E.在美术教室说的。Hannah后来也通过暗示表达类似想法，但最先明确说出“natural successor”的是Cynthia。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 9 · Conversation during the still-life lesson
quizPart1.evidence: Cynthia E. comments on Kathy as a likely successor while they work in the Art Room.

quizPart1.question: What does Ruth ask Kathy to do after the break-up?
quizPart1.questionZh: 分手后，Ruth请Kathy做什么？
options: Warn Miss Emily about a stolen tape
Ask Madame to take Tommy’s calendar
Teach Tommy the rules of chess
Talk to Tommy and help them get back together
quizPart1.explanation: Ruth appeals to Kathy’s special ability to talk to Tommy and to her loyalty. The request places Kathy inside the relationship rather than leaving her free to consider her own wishes.
quizPart1.explanationZh: Ruth希望Kathy劝Tommy复合，并强调Tommy信任她、她是可靠的朋友。这既认可Kathy，又把她放进为两人修补关系的角色中，使她自己的感情更难表达。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 9 · Ruth’s request in the dorm
quizPart1.evidence: Ruth asks Kathy to speak to Tommy on her behalf.

quizPart1.question: How does Miss Lucy’s new advice reverse her earlier reassurance to Tommy?
quizPart1.questionZh: Miss Lucy给Tommy的新建议，怎样推翻了早先的安慰？
options: She now says all guardians should stop teaching art
She now tells him that football is forbidden
She now denies ever having spoken to him
She now insists that his art matters, including for his own sake
optionsZh: 她现在说所有guardians都应停止教美术
她现在说足球已被禁止
她现在否认曾与他说过话
她现在坚持艺术很重要，也对他自己有益
quizPart1.explanation: She apologises for having discouraged his concern about creativity and urges him to make up lost time. Her reference to art as evidence remains unexplained at this point.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 她为先前让他不用担心创作而道歉，要求他补回时间，并强调艺术对他自身也重要。她提到evidence，却没有解释清楚；到第9章不要提前补入后文答案。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 9 · Tommy reports the second conversation
quizPart1.evidence: Miss Lucy tells Tommy that his art is important and that she did him a disservice before.

quizPart1.question: What are the Culture Briefings designed to practise?
quizPart1.questionZh: Culture Briefings主要让学生练习什么？
options: Judging which works Madame will select
Training as professional opera singers
Role-playing people and situations they may encounter outside Hailsham
Memorising imaginary horse pedigrees
optionsZh: 训练成为专业歌剧演员
扮演离开Hailsham后可能遇到的人与情境
背诵想象中的马的血统
quizPart1.explanation: Students role-play encounters involving figures such as café waiters and police officers. The sessions combine anticipation of outside life with anxiety about unfamiliar rules.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 他们扮演咖啡馆服务员、警察等角色，预演外界生活。这既让人期待，也让人担心：学校在训练他们适应外面，但他们对真实社会仍相当陌生。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy explains the briefings immediately before the news of Miss Lucy’s departure spreads.

quizPart1.question: Who rushes in with the news that Miss Lucy has left?
quizPart1.questionZh: 谁跑进来带来Miss Lucy离校的消息？
options: Cynthia E.
Charlotte F.
Polly T.
Marge K.
quizPart1.explanation: Charlotte F. spreads the news after another class has heard it from Miss Emily. Cynthia is associated with the earlier relationship comment, not this announcement.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 传来消息的是Charlotte F.。消息源头是Miss Emily向另一个班宣布；Cynthia E.是先前评论Kathy与Tommy关系的人，不要混淆。
quizPart1.locator: Chapter 9 · News after the Culture Briefing
quizPart1.evidence: Charlotte F. rushes into the room and reports Miss Lucy’s departure.

quizPart1.question: Which conclusion best respects what the end of Chapter 9 actually establishes?
quizPart1.questionZh: 哪项结论最尊重第9章结尾真正提供的证据？
options: Kathy is officially credited by the guardians with arranging everything
Tommy proves that his only concern was his break-up
Miss Lucy leaves, and Ruth and Tommy reunite that evening; the exact cause of her departure is not explained to the students
Miss Lucy publicly announces her full reasons in person
optionsZh: guardians正式表扬Kathy安排好了一切
Tommy证明自己唯一担心的是分手
Miss Lucy离开，Ruth与Tommy当晚复合；学生并未获知她离开的确切原因
Miss Lucy亲自公开解释所有离开原因
quizPart1.explanation: Ruth thanks Kathy, but Kathy doubts how much her intervention achieved. The sequence is clear; claims that Kathy caused every outcome or that the departure’s full explanation is already known go beyond the evidence.
quizPart1.explanationZh: 时间顺序很清楚：Miss Lucy离开，当晚Ruth与Tommy复合。但Ruth感谢Kathy，不等于Kathy就能确定自己起了决定作用；离校原因也没有向学生完整解释。要区分顺序、人物归因与确证事实。
quizPart1.evidence: Kathy reports the announcement, the same-evening reunion, and her doubt about her own influence.

part1Reference.title: Background without the date trap
part1Reference.titleZh: 背景：别混淆版本日期与首次出版

facts.en: Author: Kazuo Ishiguro. First publication: 2005.
facts.zh: 作者：Kazuo Ishiguro（石黑一雄）；首次出版：2005年。

facts.en: The supplied Vintage EPUB records a 2006 edition date and ISBN 9781400078776.
facts.zh: 你提供的Vintage EPUB标注2006年的版本日期，ISBN为9781400078776；版本日期不等于首次出版日期。

facts.en: Kathy is an adult first-person narrator recalling childhood at Hailsham. The order of memories is not a straight timeline.
facts.zh: 成年Kathy以第一人称回忆Hailsham童年；叙述常随联想跳转，章节顺序不等于完全直线的事件顺序。

facts.en: The childhood setting is a secluded school in the English countryside, within an invented social system.
facts.zh: 童年主要发生在英格兰乡间的Hailsham；小说的制度是虚构的，不能当成真实历史。

facts.en: Miss Emily: head guardian; authority, assemblies, and several major lessons.
facts.zh: Miss Emily：head guardian（首席监护人）；代表权威，主持训话，也亲自教授重要课程。

facts.en: Miss Geraldine: gentle and popular guardian; Ruth wants to feel specially favoured by her.
facts.zh: Miss Geraldine：温柔、受欢迎；Ruth渴望被她特别偏爱。

facts.en: Miss Lucy: questions how much the students understand; gives the direct speech about donations and changes her advice on art.
facts.zh: Miss Lucy：担心学生未真正理解命运；明确谈论donations，并改变了对Tommy艺术问题的建议。

facts.en: Madame: outside visitor who collects selected work; she is not one of the ordinary classroom guardians. Her precise nationality is disputed by the children.
facts.zh: Madame：从外界来挑选作品的人，不是普通授课guardian；孩子们争论她是法国人还是比利时人，不能把其猜测写成确证。

facts.en: Nurse Trisha: Crow Face, associated with frequent medical examinations. Miss Jody is mentioned about getting Tommy’s shirt clean.
facts.zh: Nurse Trisha：绰号Crow Face，负责体检；Miss Jody则与清洗Tommy的衣服有关。

part1Reference.title: Bramble, Thunder, and Daffodil
part1Reference.titleZh: 三匹马：名字、规则与顺序

facts.en: All the horses belong to a shared imaginary game, not a real school stable.
facts.zh: 这些马都属于共同的make-believe游戏，并非学校真的养了马。

facts.en: Bramble: the first horse Kathy is offered; Ruth says not to use a crop.
facts.zh: Bramble：Kathy最初获准骑的马；Ruth强调不能用crop（马鞭）。

facts.en: Thunder: Ruth’s best/favourite horse. She first says he is too dangerous, but eventually lets Kathy ride him.
facts.zh: Thunder：Ruth最好的、最喜欢的马。最初说太危险不让Kathy骑，后来还是让她骑了。

facts.en: Daffodil: Ruth tells Kathy to lean much farther back while riding her.
facts.zh: Daffodil：Ruth要求Kathy骑它时身体更向后仰。

facts.en: The game mixes real enjoyment with Ruth’s authority to grant access, dictate rules, and stop the play.
facts.zh: 游戏里有真实的快乐，也有Ruth决定资格、规则与结束时间的权力；亲密和控制并存。

part1Reference.title: Exchanges, Sales, Gallery, collections
part1Reference.titleZh: 四个概念：来源与用途不要混

facts.en: Exchanges: four per year; students’ creative work circulates through a token system.
facts.zh: Exchanges：每年四次；以学生创作为物品，用tokens交换。

facts.en: Sales: outside goods such as clothes, toys and tapes; a delivery van comes monthly. The goods arrive before the Sale itself.
facts.zh: Sales：外界的衣服、玩具、磁带等；运货车每月来。物品运到与正式Sale之间有时间间隔。

facts.en: Gallery: Madame takes selected work; its full purpose remains uncertain within Chapters 1–9.
facts.zh: Gallery：Madame拿走精选作品；在第1—9章范围内，真实用途仍未获得完整解释。

facts.en: Collections: personal possessions kept in named wooden chests under beds.
facts.zh: Collections：学生珍藏的个人物品，通常放在床下写有名字的木箱中。

facts.en: Roy J. approaches Miss Emily about tokens; Polly T. asks Miss Lucy why Madame takes the work.
facts.zh: Roy J.就tokens问题找Miss Emily；Polly T.向Miss Lucy问为什么Madame要拿走作品。

part1Reference.title: Similar names, different incidents
part1Reference.titleZh: 易混名字：连首字母与事件一起记

facts.en: Christopher C.: the Sales monitor Kathy names in her pencil-case bluff (Chapter 5).
facts.zh: Christopher C.：Kathy在笔袋事件中虚称自己与之交谈的Sales monitor（第5章）。

facts.en: Christopher H.: starts the elbow-unzipping story (Chapter 7).
facts.zh: Christopher H.：编造Tommy肘部会像拉链打开的故事（第7章）。

facts.en: Moira B.: former secret-guard member; Kathy angrily rejects her criticism (Chapter 5).
facts.zh: Moira B.：被排除的secret guard成员；批评游戏时受到Kathy反驳（第5章）。

facts.en: Midge A.: innocently asks where Ruth got her pencil case (Chapter 6).
facts.zh: Midge A.：无意中追问Ruth笔袋来源（第6章）。

facts.en: Cynthia E.: calls Kathy the likely successor to Ruth; Charlotte F.: brings the news about Miss Lucy (Chapter 9).
facts.zh: Cynthia E.：说Kathy会接替Ruth的位置；Charlotte F.：带来Miss Lucy离校消息（第9章）。

facts.en: Amanda C.: praises young Kathy’s modelling clay (Chapter 3); Patricia C.: makes the illustrated calendar (Chapter 8).
facts.zh: Amanda C.：夸Kathy的泥塑（第3章）；Patricia C.：制作有Hailsham图画的小日历（第8章）。

part1Reference.title: The secret guard and the pencil case
part1Reference.titleZh: secret guard与笔袋：别把暗示当证据

facts.en: The secret guard claims to protect Miss Geraldine from a kidnapping plot; the plot is a shared fantasy.
facts.zh: secret guard声称保护Miss Geraldine免遭绑架；阴谋是共同维持的幻想。

facts.en: Ruth pretends to know chess and gives every piece an L-shaped move. Kathy’s withdrawal is followed by exclusion from the group.
facts.zh: Ruth装作懂棋，让全部棋子按L形走；Kathy不满离开，之后被排除在小组之外。

facts.en: Ruth implies that the pencil case is a special gift without openly naming Miss Geraldine as its source.
facts.zh: Ruth暗示笔袋是特殊礼物，却没有公开明确说是Miss Geraldine送的。

facts.en: Kathy bluffs about consulting the Sales Register. She does not produce an actual record as proof.
facts.zh: Kathy虚称查过Sales Register，并没有拿出真实登记记录作证。

facts.en: When Midge asks later, Kathy protects Ruth’s mystery; neither friend can easily discuss the earlier hurt openly.
facts.zh: 后来Midge询问时，Kathy帮Ruth维持“秘密”；两人都难以直接说清先前的伤害与补偿。

part1Reference.title: The cassette: five facts to keep separate

facts.en: Singer: Judy Bridgewater. Album: Songs After Dark. Recording date given by Kathy: 1956.
facts.zh: 歌手：Judy Bridgewater；专辑：Songs After Dark；Kathy提到录制日期为1956年。

facts.en: Never Let Me Go is track three; it is a song title, not the album title.
facts.zh: Never Let Me Go是第3首歌，注意歌曲名与专辑名不同。

facts.en: Judy is pictured in a purple satin dress with a cigarette; the cigarette makes Kathy hide the cover.
facts.zh: 封面Judy穿紫色缎面裙、拿香烟；Kathy因香烟图片而隐藏封面。

facts.en: Kathy imagines a woman holding a longed-for baby, using a pillow. Madame sees her and cries; the children’s explanations remain guesses.
facts.zh: Kathy抱枕头想象一个女人终于拥有渴望的婴儿。Madame看到后哭了；孩子们对原因的解释仍是猜测。

facts.en: Ruth’s replacement is Twenty Classic Dance Tunes, not another copy of Judy’s album.
facts.zh: Ruth送的替代品是Twenty Classic Dance Tunes，不是另一盘Judy的专辑。

facts.en: The original tape disappears later; Kathy says she has no reason to link its loss to Madame’s visit.
facts.zh: 原磁带后来丢失；Kathy明确说没有理由把失窃与Madame来访联系起来。

facts.en: Peter J. speaks with Gordon about acting and America; this prompts Miss Lucy’s interruption.
facts.zh: Peter J.与Gordon谈演员梦想和美国，引发Miss Lucy打断。

facts.en: The students are fifteen during the direct speech; the elbow prank recalled in the same chapter belongs to an earlier period.
facts.zh: 直接讲话时学生15岁；同章回忆的肘部恶作剧发生得更早。

facts.en: The elbow story is a student prank. It later becomes an unzipping joke about donations, not a factual medical description.
facts.zh: 肘部故事是学生恶作剧，后来变成donations的“拉拉链”玩笑，并不是医学事实。

facts.en: Knowing a term or fact does not mean understanding what it will do to one’s life.
facts.zh: 知道一个词或事实，并不等于理解它将怎样影响自己的一生。

facts.en: After the speech, jokes fade and donation talk becomes sombre; silence can remain even when understanding grows.
facts.zh: 讲话后玩笑减少，话题变沉重；即使认识增加，沉默也可能继续。

facts.en: Room 22: Miss Lucy scribbles over blue handwriting. Kathy does not know exactly what the papers say.
facts.zh: Room 22：Miss Lucy涂黑蓝字；Kathy并不知道纸上具体写着什么。

facts.en: Patricia C.’s calendar unsettles Tommy; Kathy initially explains his mood mainly through his break-up with Ruth.
facts.zh: Patricia C.的日历令Tommy不安；Kathy最初主要用他与Ruth分手来解释情绪。

facts.en: Miss Lucy reverses her earlier art advice; Tommy is troubled by this, not only by his relationship.
facts.zh: Miss Lucy推翻早先的艺术建议；Tommy烦恼的不只是恋爱问题。

facts.en: Culture Briefings rehearse outside encounters. Charlotte F. brings the news that Miss Lucy has left; Miss Emily has announced it to another class.
facts.zh: Culture Briefings预演外界情境。Charlotte F.传来离校消息；Miss Emily已向另一个班宣布。

facts.en: Ruth and Tommy reunite that evening. Ruth credits Kathy, while Kathy is uncertain how much her intervention caused it.
facts.zh: Ruth与Tommy当晚复合。Ruth归功于Kathy，但Kathy不确定自己的劝说究竟起了多大作用。

sources.title: The Morgan Library & Museum · First-publication record
sources.note: Confirms the original London publication in 2005; distinct from the supplied Vintage edition date.

sources.title: Penguin Random House · Book information and author discussion
sources.note: Publication and English-countryside background reference. Plot details in this quiz were checked directly against the supplied EPUB.

sources.title: The Booker Prizes · Never Let Me Go
sources.note: First publication, UK publisher, 2005 shortlist and author’s 2017 Nobel Prize.

sources.title: Faber · Never Let Me Go study guide
sources.note: Publisher’s account of the early 1990 draft and later publication.

sources.title: Royal Society of Literature · Kazuo Ishiguro
sources.note: Author’s birthplace, birth date and move to Britain.

sources.title: Penguin Random House · Never Let Me Go
sources.note: Publisher-hosted introduction identifies the late-1990s English setting.

dateNote.en: For “When was the novel first published?”, answer 2005. For “When was it written?”, do not treat publication as a one-year writing period: Faber traces an early draft to 1990, followed by a pause and later reworking. The 2006 date in the supplied EPUB identifies that edition.
dateNote.zh: 问首次出版（first published）：答2005年。问创作时间（written）：不能说整本书只在2005年写成；Faber记载1990年已有早期草稿，后来搁置并重新修改。所提供EPUB中的2006年是该版本日期。

essentials.en: Kazuo Ishiguro → author; 2005 → first publication; England, late 1990s → narrative setting.
essentials.zh: Kazuo Ishiguro（石黑一雄）→作者；2005→首次出版；20世纪90年代末的英格兰→叙述背景。

essentials.en: Kathy H. → narrator, 31, a carer for over eleven years at the opening. Her memories move backwards and forwards.
essentials.zh: Kathy H.→叙述者，开篇31岁，做carer超过11年。回忆会跳转，不是严格按时间顺序讲述。

essentials.en: Miss Emily → head guardian. Miss Lucy → direct truth about donations. Miss Geraldine → popular guardian whom the secret guard protects.
essentials.zh: Miss Emily→首席监护人；Miss Lucy→直接说明捐献命运；Miss Geraldine→受欢迎、被secret guard“保护”的老师。

essentials.en: Madame → visiting art collector, not a classroom guardian. Nurse Trisha → Crow Face and medical examinations.
essentials.zh: Madame→来挑选作品的外界访客，不是课堂guardian；Nurse Trisha→Crow Face，负责体检。

essentials.en: Bramble → first horse, no crop. Thunder → Ruth’s favourite, initially refused. Daffodil → lean farther back. All three are imaginary.
essentials.zh: Bramble→先骑、不能用马鞭；Thunder→Ruth最喜欢，先不让Kathy骑；Daffodil→身体更后仰。三匹都是想象中的马。

essentials.en: Christopher C. → Sales monitor. Christopher H. → elbow prank. Midge A. → pencil-case question. Moira B. → former secret guard.
essentials.zh: Christopher C.→Sales monitor；Christopher H.→手肘拉链恶作剧；Midge A.→问笔袋来源；Moira B.→原secret guard成员。

essentials.en: Judy Bridgewater → singer. Songs After Dark → album. Never Let Me Go → track three. Twenty Classic Dance Tunes → Ruth’s replacement tape.
essentials.zh: Judy Bridgewater→歌手；Songs After Dark→专辑；Never Let Me Go→第3首歌；Twenty Classic Dance Tunes→Ruth送的替代磁带。

essentials.en: Patricia C. → calendar. Peter J. + Gordon → future dreams before Miss Lucy’s speech. Charlotte F. → news of Miss Lucy’s departure.
essentials.zh: Patricia C.→日历；Peter J.与Gordon→谈未来梦想，引出Miss Lucy讲话；Charlotte F.→传来Miss Lucy离校消息。

essentials.en: Exchanges → student work and tokens. Sales → things from outside. Gallery → selected work taken by Madame. Norfolk → the imagined lost corner.
essentials.zh: Exchanges→学生作品与代币；Sales→外界物品；Gallery→Madame带走的精选作品；Norfolk→孩子想象中收留遗失物的“失落角落”。

essentials.en: Told and not told → hearing facts without fully grasping their consequences. For analysis: detail → what it suggests → why it matters.
essentials.zh: told and not told→听过事实，却没真正理解后果。分析按：具体细节→暗示什么→为什么重要。

background.name: Author · 作者
background.en: Kazuo Ishiguro: a British novelist born in Japan. Born in Nagasaki on 8 November 1954; moved to Britain in 1960. The novel is written in English.
background.zh: 石黑一雄：出生于日本的英国小说家。1954年11月8日生于长崎，1960年移居英国；本书用英语写作。

background.name: First publication · 首次出版
background.en: 2005. The original UK publisher is Faber & Faber. Learn the year first; later editions can show different dates.
background.zh: 2005年。英国原版出版方为Faber & Faber。优先记住2005；不同版本可能标注不同日期。

background.name: Writing history · 创作过程
background.en: Faber’s study guide dates an early draft to 1990. Ishiguro set it aside and later returned to it. This is a process, not a single “written in 2005” fact.
background.zh: Faber学习指南记载1990年已有初稿，石黑一雄曾将它搁置，之后再继续修改。因此要区分创作过程与2005年出版。

background.name: Awards · 奖项
background.en: Never Let Me Go was shortlisted for the 2005 Booker Prize. Ishiguro received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2017. The Nobel recognises the author’s work, not a 2017 publication of this book.
background.zh: 《Never Let Me Go》入围2005年布克奖短名单；不是该届获奖作品。石黑一雄获得2017年诺贝尔文学奖，不表示本书在2017年出版。

background.name: Setting & structure · 背景与结构
background.en: England, late 1990s, with memories reaching back to earlier decades. Hailsham is the secluded school of Part One (Chapters 1–9). The full novel has three parts and 23 chapters.
background.zh: 开篇设定在20世纪90年代末的英格兰，回忆追溯更早年代。第一部（第1–9章）主要是封闭的Hailsham学校生活。全书共三部、23章。

background.name: Narrator & form · 叙述与文体
background.en: Kathy H.; retrospective first-person narration. She observes, remembers and guesses, rather than knowing every mind. Coming-of-age fiction combines with a dystopian/speculative setting. A memory can be vivid and still uncertain.
background.zh: Kathy H.是回顾式第一人称叙述者：她观察、回忆、推测，并非全知。小说把成长故事与反乌托邦／架空设定结合。记忆很生动，不代表每个细节或动机都完全可靠。

background.name: Opening numbers · 开篇数字
background.en: 31 years old; over eleven years as a carer already; eight more months requested, reaching almost exactly twelve years by year-end. Do not answer “already twelve years” for the opening.
background.zh: 31岁；已经当carer超过11年；还被要求继续8个月，到年底才将近整整12年。题目问开篇已工作多久，不要答“已经12年”。

background.name: Key vocabulary · 关键术语
background.en: Guardian: school adult responsible for students. Carer: supports donors. Donor: gives organs. Completed: the system’s euphemistic term for a donor’s death. The ordinary words soften the violence of the system. The word completed appears in Kathy’s adult recollection in Chapter 9.
background.zh: guardian：学校里照管学生的成人；carer：照护捐献者的人；donor：捐献器官的人；completed：制度对捐献者死亡的委婉说法。日常化词语淡化了制度的残酷。 completed一词见第9章Kathy对成年经历的回忆。

guardians.name: Miss Emily
guardians.en: The head guardian. Remember her intimidating authority, geography calendars and sex-education talks. She announces that Miss Lucy has left during a Music Appreciation class.
guardians.zh: 校长式的 head guardian。把她与威严、英格兰郡县日历、性教育讲座联系起来；第9章也是她在音乐欣赏课上宣布 Miss Lucy 已离开。

guardians.name: Miss Lucy
guardians.en: The most sporting guardian. She first reassures Tommy about not being creative; later explains the students’ predetermined futures, reverses her advice about art, and leaves Hailsham.
guardians.zh: 最擅长运动的 guardian。先安慰 Tommy 不必为缺乏创造力自责；第7章直说学生将来的命运，第9章又强调艺术重要，随后离校。

guardians.name: Miss Geraldine
guardians.en: The gentle, comforting guardian whom the younger children adore. She praises Tommy’s elephant picture. Ruth’s secret guard claims to protect her; Ruth also implies a special connection with her through the pencil case.
guardians.zh: 温柔、安慰孩子的 guardian，深受年幼学生喜爱。她表扬 Tommy 的大象画；Ruth 的 secret guard 声称保护她，Ruth 还借笔袋暗示自己受她特别关爱。

guardians.name: Madame
guardians.en: A visiting woman who selects the students’ best artwork, not an ordinary Hailsham guardian. The children test Ruth’s idea that she fears them. Kathy later finds her crying while watching the pillow dance. Her full name is not needed for Part I.
guardians.zh: 来挑选优秀作品的外来访客，不是学校日常任教的 guardian。孩子们围向她，验证 Ruth 所说的恐惧；第6章她看到 Kathy 抱枕头跳舞时落泪。第一部只需记 Madame。

guardians.name: Nurse Trisha · Crow Face
guardians.en: The nurse associated with frequent medical checks. Kathy and Tommy can talk in the queue for a check-up. Crow Face is her nickname, not a second person.
guardians.zh: 负责频繁体检的护士。Kathy与Tommy曾在等待检查的队伍中交谈。Crow Face是她的绰号，不是另一位人物。

guardians.name: Miss Jody
guardians.en: Kathy suggests that Tommy take his muddy favourite polo shirt to Miss Jody if he cannot clean it himself. The scene gives a practical association, not a stated specialist job title.
guardians.zh: 第1章 Kathy 建议：Tommy 如果自己洗不净心爱的泥污 polo shirt，可以找 Miss Jody。记住“洗衣求助”这一场景即可，不要替她编造专门职位。

guardians.name: Mr. Christopher
guardians.en: Restrains Tommy during football practice to stop him attacking Reggie D. Keep the adult title Mr. distinct from the students Christopher C. and Christopher H.
guardians.zh: 足球练习时，他按住 Tommy 的双臂，阻止他攻击 Reggie D.。注意 Mr. 是成年人称呼，别与学生 Christopher C.、Christopher H. 混淆。

guardians.name: Mr. Robert
guardians.en: Named alongside Miss Emily as an adult who often teaches art. Kathy thinks either would have told Tommy off over the elephant joke, unlike Miss Geraldine’s praise.
guardians.zh: 与 Miss Emily 一起被提到，常教美术。Kathy 认为：若大象画事件发生在他们的课上，Tommy 可能只会被训斥，不会像获得 Miss Geraldine 表扬那样引起同学的反应。

guardians.name: Mr. Roger
guardians.en: Jokes with students when Carole H. accidentally mentions the Gallery. He also teaches art. Ruth’s secret guard suspects him after watching him confer with Miss Eileen; that suspicion belongs to their fantasy.
guardians.zh: 与学生说笑时，Carole H. 不小心提到 Gallery；他也教美术。Ruth 一伙看到他与 Miss Eileen 交谈后，便把他列为“同谋”——这是孩子们的幻想，不是已证实的阴谋。

guardians.name: Mr. Frank
guardians.en: Teaches spelling in Room 9 when the children spot Madame arriving. Their excitement about the planned fear test makes his class restless.
guardians.zh: 在 Room 9 教拼写；学生看见 Madame 到来，因准备测试她是否害怕他们而坐立不安。记忆搭配：Frank → spelling → Madame 到访。

guardians.name: Miss Eileen
guardians.en: A guardian the children dislike. For a time Ruth’s secret guard imagines that she is behind a plot to kidnap Miss Geraldine. Do not present the plot as a real event.
guardians.zh: 孩子们不太喜欢的一位 guardian；secret guard 一度怀疑她是绑架 Miss Geraldine 的幕后主使。这只是他们编造、相信的故事，不是真实发生的绑架计划。

guardians.name: Mr. George
guardians.en: Teaches poetry in Room 20. This is the room where Kathy approaches Ruth’s group after their chess disagreement and realises she has been excluded from the secret guard.
guardians.zh: 在 Room 20 教诗歌。Kathy 与 Ruth 因下棋争执后，在这个教室靠近她的小团体，才意识到自己被 secret guard 排除。

guardians.name: Mr. Jack
guardians.en: Walks in on Jenny C. and Rob D. in Room 14 and sends them to Miss Emily. Remember him for this incident when revising the guardians’ awkward and inconsistent responses to sex.
guardians.zh: 在 Room 14 撞见 Jenny C. 与 Rob D. 亲密，并让两人去见 Miss Emily。这个小事件表现 guardians 对性话题的尴尬与不一致态度。

guardians.name: Mr. Chris
guardians.en: Teaches the role-play lesson just before Charlotte F. brings news of Miss Lucy’s departure. The classroom practices encounters with people outside Hailsham. This is the form of his name used in this scene.
guardians.zh: 第9章教授模拟校外生活的 role-play 课；Charlotte F. 赶来传达 Miss Lucy 离校消息时，他匆匆离开。这一场景中姓名写作 Mr. Chris。

students.name: Kathy H.
students.en: First-person narrator; thirty-one at the opening and already a carer for over eleven years. Her adult memories organise the story. At Hailsham she is observant, loyal to Ruth and able to talk closely with Tommy.
students.zh: 第一人称叙述者，开篇31岁，做 carer 已超过11年。故事由成年后的回忆串起。她善于观察，重视对 Ruth 的忠诚，也能与 Tommy 深谈。

students.name: Ruth
students.en: Kathy’s close friend and an influential group leader. Connect her with imaginary horses, the secret guard, the pencil case, and Tommy. After breaking up with Tommy she asks Kathy to help reunite them.
students.zh: Kathy 的好友，也是影响力很强的小团体领袖。把她与 imaginary horses、secret guard、笔袋和 Tommy 联系起来。第9章分手后，她让 Kathy 帮忙劝 Tommy 复合。

students.name: Tommy
students.en: Bullied for his lack of creativity and known for outbursts. Miss Lucy’s reassurance initially helps him. His art matters socially; her later reversal unsettles him. He dates Ruth, while confiding in Kathy.
students.zh: 因不擅创作而被欺负，以发脾气著称。Miss Lucy 最初的安慰使他平静；她后来改变说法又让他不安。他与 Ruth 交往，也会向 Kathy 倾诉。

students.name: Laura
students.en: The group’s comic mimic: imitates Tommy during the football humiliation and acts out touching an electric fence. In Chapter 8 she jokes about mud on Tommy’s shirt and is surprised by his anger.
students.zh: 爱搞笑、模仿别人的学生。第1章模仿 Tommy 被选队冷落时的表情，第7章模仿触电，第8章拿他背上的泥开玩笑，却意外激怒他。

students.name: Hannah
students.en: Says Graham K. has a bad temper too, so Tommy’s temper alone does not explain his bullying. Later she nudges Kathy towards the idea of becoming Tommy’s next girlfriend. Her claim linking sex to donor health is a student theory, not fact.
students.zh: 指出 Graham K. 也脾气坏，因此不能只用脾气解释 Tommy 受欺负。第9章她暗示 Kathy 可以接替 Ruth。她把性生活与捐献健康相连的说法只是学生猜测，并非事实。

students.name: Arthur H.
students.en: One of Tommy’s main tormentors. He mimics Tommy before a football free kick; the others no longer join in, showing that Tommy’s social position has begun to improve.
students.zh: Tommy 的主要欺负者之一。他在 Tommy 主罚任意球前模仿其姿势，但其他人不再响应，说明 Tommy 在同学中的处境正在好转。

students.name: Christy
students.en: Has a strong reputation for poetry, giving her enough status that even Ruth does not boss her around. Ruth later remembers that Christy moved into painting but was less successful at it.
students.zh: 以诗歌出名，地位高到连 Ruth 也不敢随便指使她。Ruth 后来回忆她转向绘画，但画得不如诗写得好。关键词：创作能力带来社会地位。

students.name: Carole H.
students.en: Accidentally mentions the Gallery while joking with Mr. Roger, then immediately covers her mouth. Her embarrassment shows the unwritten rule against discussing the Gallery in front of guardians.
students.zh: 与 Mr. Roger 说笑时不小心提到 Gallery，马上捂住嘴。她的尴尬让我们看到：在 guardians 面前谈 Gallery 有一条不成文的禁忌。

students.name: Roy J.
students.en: A year above Kathy; takes the tokens complaint to Miss Emily because Madame removes selected work without compensation. The eventual decision allows some tokens, but not many.
students.zh: 比 Kathy 高一年级。他因 Madame 带走作品却不给补偿，主动找 Miss Emily 提出 tokens 问题。最后学生获准拿到少量 tokens。

students.name: Polly T.
students.en: Asks Miss Lucy why Madame takes their work, during a library discussion of tokens. The question crosses a taboo; everyone is embarrassed but eager for an explanation.
students.zh: 在图书馆讨论 tokens 时，直接问 Miss Lucy：Madame 为什么拿走作品？问题触碰禁忌，同学一面责怪她，一面又急切想听答案。

students.name: Moira B.
students.en: An expelled former member of the secret guard. She calls the group childish and made up. Kathy, also excluded, unexpectedly defends it and invents evidence instead of joining Moira’s criticism.
students.zh: 被 secret guard 开除的前成员。她指出这游戏幼稚、都是 Ruth 编的；同样被排挤的 Kathy 却突然维护小团体，甚至编造亲耳听见阴谋的“证据”。

students.name: Marge K.
students.en: Asks whether Miss Lucy has ever smoked. The others punish her for making the situation uncomfortable, including forcing her to look towards the frightening woods from the dormitory window.
students.zh: 问 Miss Lucy 是否曾吸烟。其他人因她让场面尴尬而惩罚她，包括把她拉到宿舍窗前，逼她望向令人害怕的树林。第6章解释第5章惩罚事件的原因。

students.name: Christopher C.
students.en: The Senior monitor Kathy names when she claims to have been looking through the Sales Register. The claimed register inspection is Kathy’s bluff, not confirmed proof about Ruth’s pencil case.
students.zh: Kathy 声称查看 Sales Register 时，提到这位高年级 monitor。关键：看过登记册是 Kathy 的虚张声势，不是她真的掌握了笔袋来源的书面证据。

students.name: Midge A.
students.en: Innocently asks where Ruth got her attractive pencil case during Mr. Roger’s art lesson. Kathy helps Ruth save face instead of exposing the implication that a guardian gave it to her.
students.zh: 在 Mr. Roger 的美术课上，天真地问 Ruth 漂亮笔袋从哪里来。Kathy 这次帮 Ruth 保住面子，没有拆穿“guardian 特别赠送”的暗示。

students.name: Peter J.
students.en: Talks to Gordon about becoming actors and going to America. Miss Lucy overhears and challenges their imagined futures in her direct speech about organ donations.
students.zh: 和 Gordon 谈论当演员、去美国。Miss Lucy 听见后，直接说明学生既定的捐献命运。记忆搭配：Peter J. → Gordon → America → Miss Lucy 的讲话。

students.name: Gordon
students.en: The boy Peter J. is talking to about an acting career in America. Keep both names together when recalling the conversation that prompts Miss Lucy’s intervention.
students.zh: Peter J. 谈论赴美演艺梦想时的谈话对象。第7章诱发 Miss Lucy 直接讲话的两个男孩是 Peter J. 和 Gordon。

students.name: Christopher H.
students.en: A year above Kathy and admired by Tommy. Starts the false warning that Tommy’s elbow wound could unzip, leading Tommy to protect his arm and making him a target for teasing.
students.zh: 比 Kathy 高一年级，Tommy 很敬重他。他编造“手肘伤口会拉链式裂开”的说法，害 Tommy 小心护着手臂，成为大家的笑柄。

students.name: Gary B.
students.en: Known for a huge appetite. When he brings back a third helping of pudding, the others pretend to unzip body parts and pile them into his bowl.
students.zh: 胃口特别大。拿第三份布丁回来时，同桌同学假装把身体“拉开”、取出器官堆进他的碗里。这是 unzipping joke 后来的集体版本。

students.name: Patricia C.
students.en: Two years below Kathy and admired for drawing. Makes the small calendar of Hailsham scenes that Kathy obtains at an Exchange. Tommy reacts badly when Kathy shows it to him.
students.zh: 比 Kathy 低两年级，画技出众。她制作了画着 Hailsham 日常场景的小日历；Kathy 在 Exchange 得到后拿给 Tommy 看，却引起他的强烈反应。

students.name: Harry C.
students.en: Kathy considers choosing him as her first sexual partner because she sees him as experienced, quiet and discreet. She delays the plan; remembering her intention is different from assuming it happened.
students.zh: Kathy 曾考虑选择他作为第一次亲密关系的对象，因为觉得他有经验、安静、不会到处议论。她推迟了计划；要分清“打算”与“已经发生”。

students.name: Jenny C.
students.en: The student discovered with Rob D. by Mr. Jack in Room 14. They are sent to Miss Emily. This is Jenny C., not Jenny B., who occasionally joins the girls in the pavilion.
students.zh: 与 Rob D. 在 Room 14 被 Mr. Jack 撞见的学生，之后被叫去见 Miss Emily。不要与第1章有时加入 pavilion 聊天的 Jenny B. 混淆。

students.name: Cynthia E.
students.en: During charcoal drawing, calls Kathy the likely successor to Ruth as Tommy’s girlfriend. She is outside Kathy’s close group, which makes her comment seem like an independent observation.
students.zh: 画炭笔画时，说 Kathy 是 Ruth 之后的“自然接任者”。她不属于 Kathy 的亲密小团体，因此这句局外人的判断更让 Kathy 在意。

students.name: Charlotte F.
students.en: Rushes into the classroom with news that Miss Lucy has left. She spreads the news; Miss Emily was the guardian who originally announced it to another class.
students.zh: 冲进教室，带来 Miss Lucy 离校的消息。注意她是传消息的学生；最先在另一班正式宣布此事的 guardian 是 Miss Emily。

traps.name: Three Christophers: title and initial matter
traps.en: Mr. Christopher restrains Tommy; Christopher C. is the monitor named in the Sales Register story; Christopher H. starts the elbow prank. Do not exchange their initials or turn a student into a guardian.
traps.zh: Mr. Christopher：拦住打架的 Tommy；Christopher C.：Sales Register 说法中的 monitor；Christopher H.：手肘拉链玩笑的发起者。头衔与字母都要记准。

traps.name: Bramble / Thunder / Daffodil
traps.en: These are Ruth’s imaginary horses. Kathy rides Bramble first and must not use the crop on him. Thunder is Ruth’s favourite, initially refused but later permitted. Daffodil requires the rider to lean far back.
traps.zh: 都是 Ruth 想象中的马。Bramble：Kathy 最先骑，不能用马鞭；Thunder：Ruth 最爱，最初不让骑，后来准许；Daffodil：骑时必须大幅后仰。

traps.name: Two different token questions
traps.en: Roy J. approaches Miss Emily about compensation when Madame takes art. Polly T. asks Miss Lucy why Madame takes it at all. One concerns payment; the other concerns purpose.
traps.zh: Roy J. → Miss Emily → 被取走作品应不应该补 tokens；Polly T. → Miss Lucy → Madame 到底为什么拿作品。一个问补偿，一个问目的。

traps.name: The lost tape and Ruth’s replacement
traps.en: Singer: Judy Bridgewater. Album: Songs After Dark. Favourite song: Never Let Me Go. Ruth gives Kathy Twenty Classic Dance Tunes after the original disappears; it is not the same recording.
traps.zh: 歌手 Judy Bridgewater；专辑 Songs After Dark；最喜欢的歌 Never Let Me Go。原磁带失踪后 Ruth 送来的是 Twenty Classic Dance Tunes，并非原专辑。

traps.name: Madame’s tears: observation versus explanation
traps.en: Kathy observes Madame crying while she dances with a pillow as an imagined baby. Kathy’s interpretation and Tommy’s mind-reading suggestion are guesses. Chapters 1–9 do not settle Madame’s exact reason.
traps.zh: 可确认：Madame 看见 Kathy 抱着当作婴儿的枕头跳舞时哭了。Kathy 的解释和 Tommy 的“读心”说法都属于猜测；第1–9章没有揭晓确切原因。

traps.name: Gallery / Exchanges / Sales
traps.en: Madame selects the best work for the supposed Gallery. Exchanges occur four times yearly and use students’ creations. Sales bring objects from outside. These are three different ways objects circulate.
traps.zh: Gallery：Madame 挑走最佳作品；Exchanges：一年四次，交换学生创作；Sales：从外界运来物品供学生购买。三者不要混为一谈。

traps.name: The pencil case is an implication, not proven favouritism
traps.en: Ruth encourages the belief that Miss Geraldine gave her the pencil case. Kathy threatens that belief by pretending to have consulted the register. Neither a real gift nor an actual register inspection is established.
traps.zh: Ruth 让大家以为笔袋是 Miss Geraldine 特别送的；Kathy 假装查过登记册来动摇这个故事。不能把“确有赠送”或“Kathy 真查过册子”写成事实。

traps.name: Who announces, who carries the news?
traps.en: Miss Emily announces Miss Lucy’s departure during Music Appreciation. Charlotte F. brings the news to Kathy’s class. Mr. Chris is teaching that class. Miss Lucy herself does not give this announcement.
traps.zh: 宣布的人：Miss Emily；传到 Kathy 班上的学生：Charlotte F.；当时任课的人：Mr. Chris。不是 Miss Lucy 本人来宣布离校。

traps.name: Norfolk is a place, the lost-property story is a belief
traps.en: Miss Emily’s description of Norfolk as a lost corner becomes a student belief that lost things end up there. Hailsham also has a Lost Corner on the third floor. The imagined national collection system is not factual geography.
traps.zh: Norfolk 是真实郡名；Miss Emily 的“失落角落”说法，被学生理解成全国遗失物都会去那里。Hailsham 自己的 Lost Corner 在三楼。全国失物收集系统是孩子们的想象。

traps.name: Different Peters; similar Jennys and Sylvies
traps.en: Peter J. discusses acting; Peter N. walks with Tommy; Peter B. writes poems. Jenny B. joins pavilion chats; Jenny C. is caught with Rob D. Sylvie C. hides in a cupboard; Sylvia B. is paired with Roger D.
traps.zh: Peter J.：演员梦想；Peter N.：与 Tommy 一起走；Peter B.：写诗。Jenny B.：pavilion 聊天；Jenny C.：与 Rob D. 被撞见。Sylvie C.：躲柜子；Sylvia B.：与 Roger D. 交往。

recall.qen: First publication year, author and original UK publisher?
recall.qzh: 首次出版年份、作者和英国原版出版方？

recall.aen: 1990: early draft according to Faber. 2005: first publication. 2006: the edition date recorded in the supplied EPUB.
recall.azh: 1990：Faber所说早期草稿；2005：首次出版；2006：所提供EPUB的版本日期。

recall.qen: Who is head guardian, and who delivers the direct donation speech?
recall.qzh: 谁是首席监护人？谁直接说明捐献命运？
recall.aen: Miss Emily is head guardian. Miss Lucy gives the direct speech in Chapter 7.
recall.azh: Miss Emily是首席监护人；Miss Lucy在第7章作直接讲话。

recall.qen: Whom does the secret guard protect? What is Crow Face’s name?
recall.qzh: secret guard保护谁？Crow Face叫什么？

recall.qen: Christopher C. or Christopher H.: Sales monitor versus elbow prank?
recall.qzh: Christopher C.和Christopher H.分别与哪件事有关？
recall.aen: C. is the Sales monitor named in Kathy’s bluff; H. starts the elbow-unzipping prank.
recall.azh: C.是Kathy虚称咨询过的Sales monitor；H.编造手肘拉链的恶作剧。

recall.qen: Midge A. or Moira B.: pencil-case question versus former secret guard?
recall.qzh: 谁问笔袋来源？谁是原secret guard成员？
recall.aen: Midge A. asks about the pencil case. Moira B. is the former secret-guard member.
recall.azh: Midge A.问笔袋；Moira B.是原secret guard成员。

recall.qen: Name all three imaginary horses and one rule or distinction for each.
recall.qzh: 说出三匹想象中的马，以及各自对应的规则或细节。
recall.aen: Bramble: first, no crop. Thunder: Ruth’s favourite, first refused but eventually ridden by Kathy. Daffodil: lean farther back.
recall.azh: Bramble：先骑，不用马鞭；Thunder：Ruth最喜欢，先拒绝、后来让Kathy骑；Daffodil：身体更向后仰。

recall.qen: Singer, album, favourite track number, replacement tape?
recall.qzh: 歌手、专辑、喜欢的歌曲序号、替代磁带？
recall.aen: Judy Bridgewater; Songs After Dark; track three; Twenty Classic Dance Tunes.
recall.azh: Judy Bridgewater；Songs After Dark；第3首；Twenty Classic Dance Tunes。

recall.qen: What is the difference between an Exchange, a Sale and the Gallery?
recall.aen: Exchanges circulate students’ creative work through tokens. Sales bring in objects from outside. Madame takes selected work for the supposed Gallery.
recall.azh: Exchanges用代币交换学生作品；Sales带来外界物品；Madame挑选带走作品，学生相信它们进入Gallery。

recall.qen: Who talks about acting and America before Miss Lucy interrupts?
recall.qzh: Miss Lucy打断前，谁在谈演员与美国的梦想？
recall.aen: Peter J. and Gordon (Chapter 7). The students are fifteen at the direct speech.
recall.azh: Peter J.与Gordon（第7章）；直接讲话时学生15岁。

recall.qen: Who makes the calendar, and who brings the news that Miss Lucy has left?
recall.qzh: 谁制作日历？谁传来Miss Lucy离校的消息？
recall.aen: Patricia C. makes the calendar; Charlotte F. brings the news.
recall.azh: Patricia C.制作日历；Charlotte F.带来消息。

recall.qen: Explain “told and not told” without just repeating the phrase.
recall.qzh: 不用重复原句，解释“told and not told”。
recall.aen: Students have heard fragments about their future, but the way the information is managed prevents them from fully facing its meaning. Knowing the words is not the same as understanding the consequences.
recall.azh: 学生听过有关未来的零碎信息，但信息被控制、回避，让他们没有真正面对其意义。知道词语，不等于理解后果。

extraStudents.name: Jenny B.
extraStudents.en: Occasionally joins the girls’ pavilion conversations.
extraStudents.zh: 有时加入女孩们在 pavilion 的聊天。

extraStudents.name: Graham K.
extraStudents.en: Hannah says his bad temper makes others careful around him; this contrasts with Tommy.
extraStudents.zh: Hannah 说他的坏脾气反而让别人小心对待他，与 Tommy 形成对比。

extraStudents.name: Reggie D.
extraStudents.en: The boy Tommy tries to attack during football practice before Mr. Christopher restrains him.
extraStudents.zh: 足球练习中 Tommy 试图攻击的男孩；Mr. Christopher 把 Tommy 拦住。

extraStudents.name: Jackie
extraStudents.en: Makes the giraffes that students value at the Exchanges.
extraStudents.zh: 制作同学们在 Exchanges 喜爱的长颈鹿作品。

extraStudents.name: Susie K.
extraStudents.en: Her poems are one of the choices Kathy recalls weighing up at an Exchange.
extraStudents.zh: 她的诗是 Kathy 回忆中 Exchanges 上令人难以取舍的作品之一。

extraStudents.name: Peter B.
extraStudents.en: Writes poems that Ruth later says she probably bought because she fancied him.
extraStudents.zh: 写诗；Ruth 后来认为自己当时买他的诗，大概是因为喜欢他。

extraStudents.name: Alexander J.
extraStudents.en: Walks and chats naturally with Tommy as Tommy’s social acceptance improves.
extraStudents.zh: 与 Tommy 自然地边走边聊，显示 Tommy 逐渐被同学接纳。

extraStudents.name: Peter N.
extraStudents.en: Walks with Alexander J. and Tommy towards the fields.
extraStudents.zh: 与 Alexander J. 和 Tommy 一起走向操场。

extraStudents.name: Amanda C.
extraStudents.en: A year older than Kathy; praises young Kathy’s clay modelling as worthy of the Gallery.
extraStudents.zh: 比 Kathy 大一岁，称赞年幼 Kathy 的黏土作品足以进入 Gallery。

extraStudents.name: James B.
extraStudents.en: Tries to trip Miss Lucy during football but is himself sent flying.
extraStudents.zh: 踢球时试图绊倒 Miss Lucy，结果自己被撞飞；突出她的运动能力。

extraStudents.name: Sylvie C.
extraStudents.en: Hides in a cupboard; Miss Emily discovers her, illustrating the head guardian’s seeming awareness of everything.
extraStudents.zh: 躲进柜子，却被 Miss Emily 找到，显示校长仿佛无所不知。

extraStudents.name: Rob D.
extraStudents.en: Discovered with Jenny C. in Room 14 by Mr. Jack.
extraStudents.zh: 与 Jenny C. 在 Room 14 被 Mr. Jack 撞见。

extraStudents.name: Sharon D.
extraStudents.en: The student with whom Kathy believes Harry C. has already had sexual experience.
extraStudents.zh: Kathy 认定 Harry C. 先前已有亲密关系经验时，提到的对象是她。

extraStudents.name: Annette B.
extraStudents.en: Offers a speculative explanation for guardians’ unease about students’ sexuality; it is gossip, not verified fact.
extraStudents.zh: 对 guardians 为何不安于学生的亲密关系提出猜测；属于学生议论，并非证实的事实。

extraStudents.name: Sylvia B.
extraStudents.en: A conspicuously affectionate couple with Roger D., contrasted with Ruth and Tommy’s less showy behaviour.
extraStudents.zh: 与 Roger D. 是很爱公开亲热的一对，与不那么炫耀的 Ruth、Tommy 对比。

extraStudents.name: Roger D.
extraStudents.en: Sylvia B.’s partner in the example of a showy couple; not the guardian Mr. Roger.
extraStudents.zh: 与 Sylvia B. 组成爱炫耀亲密关系的一对；别与 guardian Mr. Roger 混淆。
